# tharsis_runner_service_account (Resource)

Assigns a service account to a runner, letting the runner authenticate as it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "tharsis_runner_service_account" "this" {
  runner_id          = tharsis_runner.this.id
  service_account_id = tharsis_service_account.this.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `runner_id` (String) The ID or TRN of the runner.
- `service_account_id` (String) The ID or TRN of the service account to assign.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) An ID for this tharsis_runner_service_account resource.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# An assignment has no identifier of its own in Tharsis. It is identified by the
# pair of resources it joins, so the id is the runner ID and the service account
# ID separated by a forward slash.
#
# Both halves must be IDs rather than TRNs. A TRN contains forward slashes of its
# own, which would make the two halves ambiguous, so TRNs are rejected with an
# explanatory error.
import {
  to = tharsis_runner_service_account.this
  id = "<runner-id>/<service-account-id>"
}

# The runner ID is shown by the "id" attribute of a tharsis_runner resource, and
# the service account ID by the "id" attribute of a tharsis_service_account
# resource. Both are also visible in the Tharsis UI.
#
# Note: the "id" attribute of this resource is generated by the provider and has
# no meaning to Tharsis, so importing produces a new value for it. That is
# expected and does not affect how the assignment is managed.
```
